title: Euler liar round predicate
statement: Given a Boolean string $z$, decode it as a pair of Boolean strings and let $N$ be the binary value of the first component. Form the encoded arithmetic quantities specified by subtracting the encoding of $(N,[\mathrm{true}])$ from the first component, reducing the binary value of the second component modulo that difference, adding the encoding of $([\mathrm{true}],\cdot)$ to obtain $A$, and then test both that the encoded greatest common divisor of $A$ and $N$ equals one and that the encoded Jacobi-symbol computation for $(A,N)$ equals the encoded modular power with base $A$ and exponent given by the tail of the difference, modulo $N$; return true exactly when both tests pass.
caveat: The statement depends on the exact meanings of the pair-decoding, binary-arithmetic encodings, Jacobi-symbol algorithm, and modular-power algorithm, which are not described in the supplied definitions.
